subject: Clarify retention windows for interaction traces (prompts vs answers)
messages:
From: Alex Klein <alex.klein@orchidanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orchid Analytics <security@orchidanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Question: default retention for prompts vs model answers?

Hi Ben —

Quick question as we're finalizing our security review: what are Redwood's default retention windows for the different pieces of an interaction? Specifically: the original customer prompt, intermediate/streamed fragments (if we use streaming), KV cache artifacts, and the final model-generated answer. Also: are attachments referenced in a request (e.g., a PDF uploaded and sent as part of the prompt) stored by default? We want concrete examples so we can map to our data retention policy.

Appreciate a short summary / examples. If helpful we can schedule a call.

Thanks,
Alex Klein
Head of Security Engineering
Orchid Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Klein <alex.klein@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-07T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: default retention for prompts vs model answers?

Alex —

Thanks for the clear question. Short answer: Redwood distinguishes transient streaming buffers, request inputs, and derived artifacts and applies different default retention windows; there are also residency and no-store controls. I've attached a short summary (redwood-retention-digest-v1.pdf) and looping in Kimberly to confirm specifics and produce an erase-evidence example.

High-level examples (defaults for hosted API, unless customer has a Private deployment or explicit flags):
- Streamed fragments / in-progress buffers: retained up to 24 hours and then purged automatically.
- Request inputs (prompts, files uploaded as part of the request): retained by default for 45 days.
- Final model outputs (generated answers): retained by default for 45 days.
- KV cache & ephemeral session state: kept in-memory for active sessions and tombstoned; short TTL (24–72 hours) unless captured explicitly by customer settings.

Attachment: redwood-retention-digest-v1.pdf (summary). Kimberly — can you add the erasure evidence path and confirm EU residency handling?

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Alex Klein <alex.klein@orchidanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: default retention for prompts vs model answers?

Alex / Ben —

Following up with the compliance-level breakdown and evidence options. I kept this focused so you can map to Orchid's policy.

1) Definitions (for clarity)
- "Request inputs": explicit user-supplied content sent in the API call (text prompts, input metadata, uploaded files referenced inline).
- "Streamed fragments": transient token buffers used to stream partial outputs; these are not the same as persisted final outputs.
- "Derived artifacts / outputs": model responses (finalized tokens), logs we persist for debugging, and any evaluation traces created by Redwood.

2) Default retention windows (hosted):
- Streamed fragments / in-flight buffers: default TTL is 24 hours; automatically purged. No customer-visible export after purge.
- Request inputs (prompts and uploaded attachment metadata/pointers): 45 days by default. Attachments uploaded as part of a request are stored for the same window unless the customer opts out. The underlying binary content is stored as an object with the same TTL and is scrubbed from the object store when purged.
- Final model outputs (answers): 45 days by default. This includes the final payload returned to the API caller.
- KV cache & session state: default tombstone TTL is 72 hours; this is primarily ephemeral and not retained for audit by default.

3) Residency and configuration options
- For EU customers we support region-scoped retention; data can be pinned to EU regions with identical default windows.
- Customers may request a "no-store" flag in the API (available on certain plans) that prevents Redwood from persisting request inputs or outputs. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can enforce their own retention via config.

4) Deletion / erase evidence process
- If Orchid requests erasure: we create an Erasure Ticket (example: HUBSPOT-54321) and run the deletion pipeline. Evidence package includes:
  - Deletion manifest with object keys and timestamps (CSV).
  - Proof-of-deletion tokens (hash list) and the job run id.
  - Confirmation email with a ticket id and timeline.
- SLA for evidence delivery: standard is 5 business days for hosted accounts; urgent/contracted SLAs can be faster (TAT negotiated in the contract).

5) Edge cases / notes
- Debugging traces: if a customer has enabled detailed debug logs, those may be retained longer in our observability backend; these are flagged and only accessible to authorized ops.
- Backups / snapshots: daily backups are retained per our backup retention policy and are overwritten per policy (not used for normal retrieval); we include backup-backport in erasure runs where applicable.

6) Actionable next steps for Orchid
- If you need legal-proof-of-delete for a full export, open an erasure request via your HubSpot contact (reply with "Erase: FULL" and we will queue HUBSPOT-54321-like job).
- If you want "no-store" behavior for production traffic, let us confirm plan and enable the flag for your org.

I can draft the short certificate of deletion (sample attached as retention-evidence-sample.txt) after the job completes.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Klein <alex.klein@orchidanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Question: default retention for prompts vs model answers?

Kim / Ben —

Thanks — that's helpful and concrete. Two quick clarifications:
1) If we request erasure for a specific user session, will the attachment object (PDF) be included in the same manifest and removed from object store?
2) In the event of a legal hold, how do you mark data to prevent automated purge?

Also please confirm the 5-business-day SLA for deletion evidence for hosted tiers (we'll flag if we need an accelerated path).

If it's easier I'd like to set a 30-minute call today to nail this down.

— Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Klein <alex.klein@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-07T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: default retention for prompts vs model answers?

Alex —

Short answers: yes, attachments included in the same erasure manifest and removed from the object store as part of the erase pipeline; and yes, we support legal-hold markers — those are applied as a hold tag on the tenant and suspend automated purges until released.

Kim — can you kick off a short runbook note for Alex on how to open the erase request and what the evidence package will look like? I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute call at 14:00 PT if that works for you, Alex.

Attaching: retention-evidence-sample.txt (illustrative output for an erase run).

Best,
Ben
